question: Capocollo di Martina Franca is one of the Apulian culinary tradition’s most time-honoured and iconic delicacies. Based on practices that have been handed down over generations in the Valle d’Itria, Capocollo’s artisanal production process is a particularly significant part of the area’s cultural and economic heritage.

In February 2024, the Italian authorities sent the Commission a request to recognise Capocollo as a PGI. Further clarification and supporting documents were submitted in 2024 and 2025 as part of the relevant assessment procedure.

It should also be noted that the competent Italian administrative court issued a definitive ruling on 30 October 2025 in which it determined that the decision confirming the full legitimacy of Capocollo’s designation procedure had acquired the force of res judicata. In the light of the above: 1.
Is the Commission still in the process of assessing the application to register Capocollo di Martina Franca as a PGI?
What are the next stages that applications like the above typically have to go through as part of the registration process?

Given that, as mentioned above, the relevant additional documentation supporting the application has already been submitted, could the Commission estimate how long it will take to complete this registration procedure and publish the resulting PGI single document in the Official Journal?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.7.

2026) Following the completion of the Commission’s scrutiny of the application for registration of the name ‘Capocollo di Martina Franca’ as a protected geographical indication (PGI) since, according to the Commission, the application fulfils the conditions referred to in Article 15(1) and (4) of Regulation (EU) 2024/11431, it has been published for opposition in the Official Journal (C series) of the European Union on 22 June 20262.

This publication will open a three-month opposition period. If no admissible reasoned statement of opposition is received within this period, the Commission will then launch the adoption procedure for the Commission Implementing Regulation on the registration of the geographical indication and finally publish it in the Official Journal (L series).
The completion of the registration process usually takes four to six additional weeks after the end of the publication period.
